key_insight: ToolSmith proposes automatically generating tools for multimodal search agents instead of relying solely on a fixed, hand-crafted toolkit. The core idea is to let agents adapt their capabilities as unfamiliar search needs arise.
problem_solved: Hand-crafted search and visual tools are costly to build and maintain, and fixed tool libraries struggle with new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes.
method: Introduce an automatic tool-generation framework for multimodal search agents.
Motivate tool creation through the human practice of fashioning new tools from familiar components.
Support reasoning, vision, and live web search workflows; implementation details and evaluation are not provided in the supplied abstract excerpt.
impact: Automatic tool generation could reduce manual toolkit maintenance and make search agents more adaptable. The supplied excerpt does not establish measured performance gains.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed hand-crafted toolkit versus an expandable, automatically generated toolkit.
Conceptual workflow: unfamiliar query → capability gap → tool generation → multimodal search.
Component illustration showing familiar tool parts assembled into a new tool.
Icons representing reasoning, vision, live web search, and diverse evidence formats.
paper_title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
paper_authors: Rui Sun, Junhua Huang, Luca Zancato, Md Mofijul Islam, Kai-Wei Chang
